name: Account takeover
plainEnglish: A criminal gets into a real customer's account and uses it as if they were the customer.
warningSigns: A device the customer has never used before
Password, email or phone number changed shortly before a payment
A new payee followed quickly by a large withdrawal
Activity at an unusual time for this customer
howToRespond: Stop the payment and contact the customer on details held before the recent changes.

name: Genuine customer: travelling abroad
plainEnglish: A real customer spending in another country. A foreign location on its own is not fraud.
warningSigns: Same trusted device as always
Spending that fits a trip: hotels, transport, food
No recent changes to login or contact details
Earlier travel bookings on the account
howToRespond: Approve. Declining leaves a real customer stranded without money abroad.

name: Crypto cash-out to a fresh wallet
plainEnglish: Stolen or fraudulent funds are converted to crypto and sent to a brand-new wallet, where they are very hard to recover.
warningSigns: A very new account with deposits but no normal activity
Several different cards funding one account
Withdrawal of nearly the whole balance soon after deposit
Destination wallet created very recently or linked to risky wallets
howToRespond: Hold the withdrawal and review where the deposits came from before any funds leave.

name: Card testing
plainEnglish: A criminal who has a card number makes tiny payments to find out whether the card works before using it for something bigger.
warningSigns: Several very small payments in a few minutes
Different online merchants the customer has never used
Refused attempts with a wrong security code or expiry date
Activity while the customer would normally be asleep
howToRespond: Decline, block the card and send the customer a replacement.

name: Genuine customer: big one-off purchase
plainEnglish: A real customer making an unusually large payment for something planned. A high amount on its own is not fraud.
warningSigns: Earlier deposit or contact with the same merchant
Customer moved their own money in to cover it
Usual device and usual location
Customer can explain the purchase in detail
howToRespond: Approve. Blocking a planned purchase is frustrating and can cost the customer their order.

name: Genuine customer: new phone
plainEnglish: A real customer who has replaced their phone. A new device matters most when other details change with it.
warningSigns: No change to password, email or phone number
Same home location as before
Payment to a long-standing payee
Amount and timing match the customer's routine
howToRespond: Approve. Look for a new device combined with other changes before treating it as a takeover.
